headline: Software Holds the Line as Sellers Dominate a Bruising Thursday Session
body_html:
With the Thursday, October 1 session still in progress, the tape is running decidedly negative. Of 544 names tracked across our universe, 363 are in the red against just 177 in positive territory, and the damage is spread wide. Homebuilders lead the decline, off 1.29%, followed by Industrials at minus 1.02%. Healthcare and Consumer names are also under meaningful pressure, surrendering 0.75% and 0.72% respectively, as risk appetite retreats ahead of the close.

The sole sector holding its head above water is Software, which is posting a modest gain of 0.43% on the day. Cybersecurity name Qualys and EDA specialist Synopsys are each up roughly 5%, while automation software firm UiPath and ZoomInfo add more than 4% apiece. The gains point to selective appetite for technology with visible recurring-revenue characteristics even as the broader market struggles. The standout mover, however, sits outside software entirely: Rogers Corp, the electronic-materials specialist, has surged 10.73%, the sharpest advance in the universe mid-session.

On the downside, Jabil has shed more than 10%, making it the session's most punishing decliner. Geopolitical friction — tanker strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, rising Middle East tensions, and a spike in UK long-dated gilt yields to levels not seen since 1998 — is weighing on sentiment. Traders should watch whether Software's thin lead holds as late-session macro headlines have a history of reshuffling sector standings near the close.

briefs.headline: Rogers Corp Surges More Than 10% to Top the Leaderboard
briefs.body: Electronic-materials maker Rogers Corp is the standout gainer in our universe mid-session, up 10.73%. The move is sharp enough to draw attention from momentum-oriented desks, though no formal catalyst has been confirmed. Fellow tech-adjacent name FormFactor is not far behind, climbing 9.59% in semiconductor-equipment trading.

briefs.headline: Jabil Slides 10% in Heaviest Single-Stock Decline of the Day
briefs.body: Electronics-manufacturing specialist Jabil is the session's deepest loser, off 10.03% with the session still open. The drop stands out even against a broadly negative tape, suggesting company-specific news or guidance pressure rather than purely macro selling. Inspire Medical Systems follows with a 5.22% retreat in the Healthcare-Devices space.

briefs.headline: UK 30-Year Gilt Yields Clear 6% for First Time Since 1998
briefs.body: British long-dated sovereign borrowing costs have broken above the 6% threshold, a level not touched since the late 1990s. The move is amplifying global risk-off sentiment and drawing comparisons to prior episodes of fiscal concern in developed markets. Currency and fixed-income traders are watching for spillover into equities.

briefs.headline: Tanker Strikes Near the Strait of Hormuz Lift Oil Prices
briefs.body: Three oil tankers were struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz earlier this week, according to shipping risk firm Marisk. The incidents, combined with China suspending fuel exports, have pushed crude prices roughly 2% higher on the day. Energy equities in our universe are nonetheless down 0.40%, suggesting the oil move has not yet translated into equity relief.

briefs.headline: SpaceX Prepares to Carry Google AI Chips Into Orbit
briefs.body: A SpaceX mission is being readied to deliver Google-developed artificial-intelligence chips to orbit as part of a broader push toward space-based data-center infrastructure. The launch underscores accelerating commercial demand for compute capacity beyond terrestrial limits. Satellite and adjacent technology names are among the market's areas of investor focus this session.

briefs.headline: Japan's Premier Signals Policy Commitment to Yen Stability
briefs.body: Japan's prime minister stated that her government's policies are designed to rebuild confidence in the yen following a period in which U.S. intervention efforts fell short of market expectations. The remarks come as currency volatility remains elevated across major pairs. Investors with cross-border exposure are monitoring Tokyo's policy posture heading into the weekend.
